semantic_correction.stem: A healthy pregnant client with an uncomplicated pregnancy asks about exercise. Which recommendation is most appropriate?

options.A: Avoid beginning aerobic activity during pregnancy if you were sedentary before conception and wait until after delivery.
options.B: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity each week and start gradually if you are new to exercise.
options.C: Use vigorous-intensity exercise as the preferred starting level even if you did not exercise vigorously before pregnancy.
options.D: Keep the same exercise routine throughout pregnancy without adjustment because pregnancy-related changes do not affect activity choices.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current ACOG guidance states that, in an uncomplicated pregnancy without medical or obstetric contraindications, physical activity is safe and desirable. Pregnant clients should ideally obtain at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity each week. ACOG also states that clients who are new to exercise should start slowly and gradually increase activity. People who were habitually vigorous exercisers before pregnancy may often continue vigorous activity with appropriate obstetric guidance, but vigorous exercise is not the default starting prescription for previously inactive clients, and exercise may require adjustment as pregnancy progresses.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Counsel a healthy client with an uncomplicated pregnancy to obtain at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity weekly, with gradual progression when new to exercise.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: shortened the uniquely long correct answer, retained the ACOG 150-minute target and gradual progression advice, and removed claims that sedentary clients must wait until postpartum or that exercise never requires pregnancy-specific adjustment.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests current exercise guidance for uncomplicated pregnancy with balanced alternatives and no universalization of vigorous exercise or inactivity.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. ACOG supports gradual initiation of exercise in previously sedentary clients when pregnancy is uncomplicated and no contraindication exists.
option_audit.B: Correct. It matches the current ACOG weekly target and gradual-start recommendation.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Vigorous activity is not the preferred starting level for a client who was not previously exercising vigorously.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Pregnancy-related physiologic changes and clinical status can require modification of exercise.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. B alone combines the correct weekly target and progression advice for a healthy uncomplicated pregnancy.
cueing_check: All four options are exercise recommendations of comparable length and specificity; no unique-length or absolute-word cue identifies B.
